m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series (pre-game through close)
m.quote_history.mechanism: The market's own price path aggregates information (injury news, lineup confirmation, sharp flow) and defines the executable price at each decision time.
m.quote_history.rationale: Quote history is the only way to know what price was actually available at the decision timestamp, to measure line moves against injury-report vintages, and to separate stale quotes from real information. Subtle: last-trade prints on thin NBA prop rungs can be hours old, so mid-of-bid-ask with a staleness flag is safer than last price; and any model input must be joined point-in-time to a quote vintage, never to a closing price.
m.quote_history.measurement: Store every candlestick/snapshot with exchange timestamp and retrieval timestamp. Features: mid, spread, time since last trade, move since open, move in the 90 minutes before tip, move conditional on a news event. Join model features as-of (<= quote time).
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine how much size can be filled at the quoted price and how large the round-trip cost is.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: A mispricing smaller than the half-spread plus fee is not tradable. NBA player-prop rungs far from the main line are often wide and thin, so apparent edges there are frequently untradable. Depth also signals market-maker confidence: a quote that collapses in size near tip often precedes lineup news.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Per rung: best bid/ask, size at best, cumulative size within 2c and 5c, spread in cents and as fraction of price; time-weighted averages over the last hour before tip.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Traded volume and open interest proxy for how much information and how many informed participants have priced the market.
m.volume_oi.rationale: Higher-volume main lines (star player points, game spread) tend to be better arbitraged than thin alternate rungs, so the same model edge should be discounted differently by liquidity. Open interest growth through the day also indicates when the market is still absorbing news. Subtle: volume is cumulative and includes both sides, so use deltas around events.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Cumulative and per-hour volume, open interest, number of distinct trade prints; rank of the rung within its event by volume; ratio of volume to open interest.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: A strike ladder is a set of tail probabilities of one underlying count; consistency across rungs exposes mispriced rungs and reveals the market's implied distribution.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Over/under ladders (e.g. points 15+/20+/25+/30+) must be monotone non-increasing, and the implied pmf (differences between rungs) shows where the market puts mass. Rungs are heavily correlated, so a model edge on 25+ is largely the same bet as on 30+; position sizing must treat the ladder as one exposure. Also reveals integer-vs-half-point structure and whether the market's implied variance is wider or narrower than a count model.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Extract all rungs for the same player/stat/game, enforce monotonicity, difference to get implied P(X=k), fit mean and dispersion; flag rungs whose price is off the fitted curve by more than spread+fee; compute rung correlation for exposure netting.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: The realized outcome and settlement timestamp are the ground truth the whole backtest is scored against.
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Needed for calibration and hit-rate work but never a pregame input. Subtle: NBA box scores are occasionally corrected after the game (assist, rebound, steal credit), and Kalshi settles on a defined source/time, so the settled value can differ from a later-corrected box score; labels must come from the contract settlement, not a re-scraped box score.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Pull settled value, result, settlement time per market; reconcile with the box score source named in the rules; flag disagreements and late changes.

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement, void)
m.rules_text.mechanism: Contract wording determines what event is being predicted: whether overtime counts, how DNP or postponement resolves, push handling, and which stat source governs.
m.rules_text.rationale: The same basketball outcome can map to different payouts depending on wording: overtime-inclusive totals shift the total by roughly the OT probability times about 10 points; player props may void or settle No on DNP; period markets may exclude OT. A model fitted on the wrong settlement definition is systematically biased. Wording can differ between series and change over time, so version it per market.
m.rules_text.measurement: Snapshot rules_primary / rules_secondary text per market with hash; parse flags: ot_included, dnp_rule (void vs No), postponement_rule, tie_rule, source_of_truth, strike inclusivity (> vs >=).

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sportsbook lines are an independent, highly liquid estimate of the same distribution and embed information (injuries, sharp money) that fundamentals miss.
m.external_lines.rationale: For NBA sides and totals the sharp closing line is hard to beat; for player props it is a strong prior on the mean and distribution. The informative quantity is the disagreement between Kalshi and the book after removing vig, and whether the book moved first. Subtle: timestamps must be point-in-time and props are often posted/stale at different times than main lines.
m.external_lines.measurement: De-vig each book line (multiplicative or power), convert to implied mean/probability, track open-to-now movement and cross-book dispersion; compute Kalshi minus consensus per rung with staleness flags.

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force
m.fees.mechanism: Fees convert a model probability edge into an expected net return and vary with price.
m.fees.rationale: The fee is a function of price (largest near 50c), so the minimum edge required differs by rung: a 2c edge can be profitable on a 10c longshot and negative at 50c. The schedule can change and differs for maker vs taker orders, so it must be versioned.
m.fees.measurement: Versioned fee formula per series; net edge = model p - price - fee(price) for taker, with maker rebate/fee where applicable; breakeven edge by price bucket.

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: Market open, close, halt and postponement events define when information can still be traded on and when a market is void.
m.lifecycle.rationale: NBA markets may close at tip or stay open into play; a lineup surprise after close cannot be traded, and postponed games void or extend. Determining the true last tradable time per market is required for point-in-time discipline.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Record open_time, close_time, expected_expiration, status transitions with timestamps; compute minutes between last injury-report update and close; flag postponed or rescheduled games.

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung per family (from settlements)
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Empirical hit rates by rung reveal systematic miscalibration of the market in that family (favorite-longshot, over bias) independent of any fundamentals model.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: If 30+ point rungs priced at 12c hit 9% over a large sample, that is a calibration finding that stands without a player model. Subtle: rungs on one game are correlated, so effective sample size is the number of games not markets, and hit rates must be conditioned on price bucket and line vintage.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: From settled markets: realized frequency vs mean price by price bucket, by strike distance from the book mean, by family and season; bootstrap by game for intervals.

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time) for slippage and flow
m.trade_tape.mechanism: The trade tape shows realized execution prices, aggressor side and size, giving slippage and informed-flow signals.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Large taker prints preceding a line move are a candidate informed-flow signal, and the tape sets realistic fill assumptions. Subtle: in thin NBA markets a single print can be a retail order, so it needs size and repeat-flow filters.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Per trade: price, size, taker side, timestamp; features: signed volume imbalance in trailing windows, VWAP vs mid, price impact of prints, time to next print.

nba.stat_corrections.label: Post-game stat corrections and source-of-truth lag
nba.stat_corrections.mechanism: The settlement source can change after the game (scorer corrections to assists, rebounds, steals, minutes), which changes the realized label for razor-thin rungs.
nba.stat_corrections.rationale: Official NBA stat corrections occur within hours and sometimes days; a Kalshi settlement might use the figure at a defined time. Props sitting exactly at the line are exposed. Knowable pregame only as a historical base rate of corrections by stat type and arena, not for a given game.
nba.stat_corrections.measurement: From archived box scores at game end vs 24-48h later, compute correction frequency by stat and arena; read rules_text for source and settlement timing; flag rung-at-threshold exposure.

nba.market_calibration_bias.label: Price-bucket miscalibration (favorite-longshot, over bias) in NBA families
nba.market_calibration_bias.mechanism: Retail participation patterns can leave systematic bias by price level and direction (e.g. overs on star props) that shows up as a reliability-curve gap.
nba.market_calibration_bias.rationale: Distinct from fundamentals: a reliability curve per family and side tells how much to shade model probabilities toward or away from price. Highly regime-dependent and a pure hypothesis until tested on out-of-sample seasons. Must separate calibration at the rung level from game-level correlation.
nba.market_calibration_bias.measurement: Reliability curves (realized vs implied, 5c buckets) per family x side x main-line/alt-rung, using de-vigged book lines as the reference; calibration slope/intercept with game-clustered intervals.

nba.implied_team_totals.label: Market-implied team points from spread and total
nba.implied_team_totals.mechanism: Spread and total jointly imply each team's expected points, which translate into possessions and efficiency for every player in that game.
nba.implied_team_totals.rationale: Team implied total = (total ± spread)/2. Player props (points, assists, rebounds, threes) scale with team points and with the game's pace, and the implied totals move on injury news before box-score features update. It is the compact summary of the book's view of pace and offense in this exact matchup with current availability.
nba.implied_team_totals.measurement: implied_home = (T - S)/2 and implied_away = (T + S)/2 where S is home spread (negative = home favorite); deviation from the team's season average points; movement since open.

nba.off_rtg.label: Opponent-adjusted offensive rating, lineup-adjusted
nba.off_rtg.mechanism: Points scored per 100 possessions, adjusted for opponent defense, venue and the current available roster, is the core of the expected scoring margin and total.
nba.off_rtg.rationale: Raw team ratings mix opponents and rosters; the relevant quantity is the rating of the lineup that will play tonight. Subtle: early-season and post-trade ratings are noisy and must be shrunk to a prior (preseason projection plus player-based estimate); recency weighting should favor games with the current core healthy; garbage-time possessions should be filtered.
nba.off_rtg.measurement: Ridge-regress game-level ORtg/DRtg on offense/defense/home dummies over a rolling window with exponential decay; filter garbage time (Cleaning-the-Glass-style rules from play-by-play); shrink toward preseason prior with weight growing with possessions; adjust for tonight's missing players using player on/off or RAPM values.

nba.def_rtg.label: Opponent-adjusted defensive rating
nba.def_rtg.mechanism: Points allowed per 100 possessions adjusted for opponent offense and current roster determines how much the opponent's offense is suppressed.
nba.def_rtg.rationale: Defense is noisier than offense over short windows because opponent shooting luck (esp. opponent 3P% on open looks) is a large share of variation; ratings should be partly shrunk toward shot-quality-based expectation. Rim protector availability swings defensive rating more than any other single absence.
nba.def_rtg.measurement: Same ridge setup as offense on defensive rating; blend observed DRtg with expected DRtg from opponent shot quality allowed (location, openness); recency decay; adjust for tonight's absent rim protectors/wing stoppers via on/off.

nba.pace.label: Pace/possessions, opponent-adjusted, lineup-aware
nba.pace.mechanism: Possessions per game scale every counting stat and the total; the game's pace is a joint outcome of both teams' preferences and the lineups on the floor.
nba.pace.rationale: Pace is not additive: expected game pace is roughly league average plus each team's deviation, but slower teams usually win the tempo contest on defense and transition-heavy teams are constrained by opponent make-rates. Lineup changes (a primary ball-pusher out) shift pace. Blowouts and intentional fouling alter late possession counts.
nba.pace.measurement: Regress per-game possessions on team-offense and team-defense pace effects (or compute expected pace = league + (paceA - lg) + (paceB - lg)); filter to competitive minutes; lineup-adjust using on/off pace; compare to market implied total via possessions x efficiency.

nba.ratings.label: Team ratings / schedule strength for season markets
nba.ratings.mechanism: A season-level team rating (net rating plus roster talent plus health) feeds simulations for wins, seed, series and title.
nba.ratings.rationale: Season markets require a rating that combines prior-season performance, roster changes, current-season results and injury information; single-season net rating has meaningful luck variance. Subtle: ratings should reflect playoff-relevant strength (top-8 rotation health) rather than regular-season depth for title/series markets, and be uncertainty-aware.
nba.ratings.measurement: Bayesian team rating: preseason prior from player-based projection (minutes-weighted EPM/BPM/RAPM) updated by game results with margin capped and garbage filtered; produce mean and sd; separate regular-season and playoff rotation versions.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.label: Availability-adjusted team rating for tonight's active set
nba.lineup_adj_rating.mechanism: Team strength given who is actually active, computed by summing player impact over expected minutes, moves spreads, totals and every player prop in the game.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.rationale: A star absence changes team net rating by an amount far larger than most other features; the market reprices within minutes of the report. The model needs an independent player-impact valuation to avoid just reading the market. Subtle: impact of replacing a player is not the star's full value (usage redistributes), and replacement is nonlinear when multiple players are out.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.measurement: Sum over expected-minute allocation of per-player impact (RAPM/EPM/BPM shrunk) for the active set vs team average-active baseline; difference gives point-spread adjustment; validate with with/without team splits when sample allows.

nba.player_impact.label: Player impact value (RAPM/BPM/EPM-style) with shrinkage
nba.player_impact.mechanism: A shrunk player-level impact estimate converts availability changes into rating changes and anchors projections for newly acquired or returning players.
nba.player_impact.rationale: On/off splits alone are noisy; regularized adjusted plus-minus blended with box-score priors (BPM) gives more stable estimates. Used for lineup_adj_rating, awards and futures. Subtle: impact is context-dependent (lineup partners, role), aging, and minutes restrictions after injury.
nba.player_impact.measurement: Multi-year ridge RAPM with box-score prior, age curve and minutes-weighted shrinkage; separate offensive and defensive components; recency weighting of current season.

nba.venue.label: Arena/home-court effect
nba.venue.mechanism: Home court raises scoring margin through crowd, travel asymmetry, familiarity and referee behavior; the magnitude differs by arena and has changed over time.
nba.venue.rationale: League-wide NBA home advantage has been around 2-3 points but has varied and arena-specific effects (altitude, crowd) are small relative to noise, so team-specific home edges should be heavily shrunk. Neutral venues (Cup knockout, international games, Mexico City/Paris) need explicit treatment.
nba.venue.measurement: Estimate league home advantage per season by regression; team-specific deviation with strong shrinkage; flag neutral sites and international games.

nba.rest_travel.label: Rest, back-to-back, travel, altitude
nba.rest_travel.mechanism: Fatigue from short rest, back-to-backs and dense schedule modestly lowers efficiency and, through coaching decisions, changes minutes and availability.
nba.rest_travel.rationale: Rest effects on team performance are small but real; larger is the indirect channel where stars sit on the second night of a back-to-back, which is handled by availability inputs. Rest differential (not absolute rest) matters for the spread; 3-in-4 and 4-in-6 clusters, and games after long road trips, add tail risk. Subtle: effect sizes have shrunk in the sports-science era and must be fit on recent seasons only.
nba.rest_travel.measurement: Per team: days of rest, is_b2b, second_game_of_b2b_on_road, games in last 4/6/7 days, rest differential; interactions with age and minutes load; fit effect on margin residual vs closing line.

nba.travel_altitude.label: Travel distance, time zones, and altitude (Denver, Utah)

nba.travel_altitude.rationale: Altitude at Denver and Utah is the main environment effect hypothesized to matter in late-game fatigue; coast-to-coast trips with a day-game next stop are another. Effects likely small and can be absorbed by the market line, so mainly useful for second-order effects on totals and fourth-quarter minutes.
nba.travel_altitude.measurement: Great-circle distance since last game, time-zone shift, altitude of venue, interactions with is_b2b; evaluate residual vs line by period (late-game efficiency, Q4 scoring).

nba.standings_motivation.label: Standings, clinch/tank incentives and late-season motivation
nba.standings_motivation.mechanism: Teams out of contention or with locked seeds rest stars or play young players, changing availability and minutes distribution late in the season.
nba.standings_motivation.rationale: Late-season and post-clinch games show elevated load management and unpredictable rotations, making both sides and player props noisier and shifting minutes to bench players. Subtle: announcements arrive late (game-day), and tanking incentives (lottery odds) differ from effort incentives; play-in positioning and in-season Cup stakes alter incentives too.
nba.standings_motivation.measurement: Compute win-probability leverage per game from standings simulation (seed distribution sensitivity), clinch/elimination flags, games remaining, lottery odds sensitivity; interact with star age/injury history.

nba.referee_crew.label: Referee crew tendencies (fouls, pace, total, home bias)
nba.referee_crew.mechanism: The assigned crew's foul-calling rate sets free-throw volume, foul trouble, and game pace, affecting totals and certain player props.
nba.referee_crew.rationale: Crew assignments are public the morning of game day, so they are knowable but the effect is modest and the historical estimate noisy; crews with higher foul rates raise free-throw attempts and lower fluidity. nba.fouls_ft.label: Foul drawing, free-throw rate and officials/referee crew
nba.fouls_ft.mechanism: Team and player foul-drawing rates and opponent foul-committing rates determine free-throw volume, an efficient scoring source that influences points and total.
nba.fouls_ft.rationale: FT rate is more stable than FT% and differs strongly by player role (rim attackers, bigs). Opponent foul rate allowed matters but is scheme-dependent (drop vs switching). Crew effect (see referee_crew) interacts. Subtle: FT attempts counted in totals but also lengthen games, and intentional fouling late skews FTA in blowouts/close games.

nba.def_scheme.label: Team defensive scheme and play-type profile (drop, switch, blitz, zone)
nba.def_scheme.mechanism: Scheme determines which shots and passes are conceded, shaping opponent guard assists, big-man rebounds/scoring and three-point volume.

nba.three_pt_luck.label: Team three-point shooting luck vs shot quality (own and opponent)
nba.three_pt_luck.mechanism: Realized team 3P% regresses toward a shot-quality-based expectation; opponent 3P% allowed is mostly outside the defense's control on open looks.
nba.three_pt_luck.rationale: Hot or cold shooting streaks inflate or deflate recent offensive/defensive ratings and totals; ignoring regression overstates how hot teams will score and how stingy lucky defenses are. Subtle: shooters' true skill still differs, so expectation must use shooter-specific priors and shot openness, not a league mean.
nba.three_pt_luck.measurement: Expected 3P% = sum over attempts of shooter prior (career/regressed) adjusted for openness; luck = actual - expected over trailing N games; estimate shrinkage factor from out-of-sample reversion; same for opponent 3P% allowed with league-mean prior weighted heavily.

nba.pythag_residual.label: Point-differential vs record luck (Pythagorean residual, clutch record)
nba.pythag_residual.mechanism: Wins above point-differential expectation (close-game results) mean-revert, so records overstate or understate true strength for futures and win totals.
nba.pythag_residual.rationale: Records built on unusual clutch/close-game results are less predictive than margin-based ratings. Used mainly for season wins, seeds and playoff futures; also reveals when a market anchored to the standings misprices the true team. Subtle: coaching/late-game execution may have a small persistent component, so shrink rather than zero it out.
nba.pythag_residual.measurement: Pythagorean wins with exponent ~14 (fit by season) minus actual; clutch (score within 5, last 5 min) record vs expectation; apply 50% or fitted regression to remaining games.

nba.score_resid.label: Score residual distribution around lines
nba.score_resid.mechanism: The distribution of actual margin/total minus the closing line gives the variance, skew and tail mass needed to convert a point-spread/total edge into a probability.
nba.score_resid.rationale: NBA margin sd around the closing spread is roughly 11-12 points and total sd roughly 17-19; these differ by spread size (blowouts have fatter tails), pace and period. Subtle: the center of the residual distribution is zero if lines are efficient, so the use is the shape (variance by line size, push masses at integer numbers) rather than bias.
nba.score_resid.measurement: Compute empirical residual distribution of (margin + spread) and (total points - total) over multiple seasons by spread bucket and total bucket; fit scale; compute probability mass at integers for push/at-threshold handling.

nba.garbage.label: Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread
nba.garbage.mechanism: The probability and timing of a lopsided margin determine starter minutes loss, bench usage, and distortions to late scoring and period totals.
nba.garbage.rationale: Large pregame spreads and in-game leads cut starters' minutes (stars often finish 4-8 minutes below expectation in blowouts), reducing counting stats; this is the main reason high spreads depress over rates on star props. nba.ot_model.label: Overtime probability and minutes
nba.ot_model.mechanism: Regulation ties send games to overtime (about 5-6% of games), adding about 5 minutes and typically ~10-12 points to totals and some player stats.
nba.ot_model.rationale: OT probability rises for tight spreads and low-scoring, slow games, and matters for markets that include OT in settlement (totals, spreads, player props) versus those that exclude it (period markets, some race-to markets). Subtle: probability is nearly flat across spreads under ±6, so the key is wording, not a precise model.

nba.late_game_script.label: Late-game foul and clock-management script
nba.late_game_script.mechanism: In close games the trailing team fouls intentionally and the leader attempts free throws, which inflate totals and free-throw counts; in blowouts clocks run out.
nba.late_game_script.rationale: This creates asymmetry between spreads/totals covers (a late garbage-time basket can flip a cover) and affects period-4 markets and FT props. nba.status_resolution_prob.label: Probability a questionable/GTD player plays (calibrated)

nba.status_resolution_prob.rationale: Using 'questionable' as a coin flip loses information: historical play rates depend on injury body part, whether the player practiced, team, rest day, stakes, and whether the player was already ruled 'probable' earlier. nba.pot_ast.mechanism: Potential assists (passes that lead to a shot attempt) are the opportunity count; actual assists are potential assists times teammate make probability.

nba.teammate_conv.label: Teammate shot conversion / shooting quality
nba.teammate_conv.mechanism: Assists depend on whether the shots a player creates are made; the shooting skill and shot quality of teammates on the floor raises or lowers conversion.
nba.teammate_conv.rationale: Teammate expected eFG on the passes created (shooters like catch-and-shoot specialists vs low-percentage players) changes assists per potential assist from ~0.4 to ~0.6. nba.reb_chances.label: Rebound chances and contested rebounds
nba.reb_chances.mechanism: Rebounds are opportunity (chances) times conversion; chances depend on position on the floor, teammates' rebounding and the volume of missed shots.

nba.rebound_pool.label: Rebound pool: expected missed shots in the game by type
nba.rebound_pool.mechanism: Total available rebounds equal both teams' missed field goals and free throws; pace and shooting efficiency determine the pool, and shot type changes where rebounds go.
nba.rebound_pool.rationale: A high-pace, low-efficiency game produces many missed shots and more rebounds per player. season_futures_team.mechanism: Probabilities come from a simulation: team ratings with uncertainty updated through the season, the remaining schedule with rest and home/away, injury scenarios for key players and the official tiebreaker/play-in structure; the playoffs add bracket path and series models with playoff-tightened rotations. Win-total and seed markets are sensitive to rating uncertainty and boundary effects; title odds are convex in star health. Market prices incorporate narratives; edges come from uncertainty handling, luck regression and rule boundaries.

series_and_cup.target: Series winner, series length / sweep, and NBA Cup winner/stage outcomes
series_and_cup.mechanism: A best-of-seven series is a sequence of correlated games with 2-2-1-1-1 home structure and playoff-tightened rotations; probability of winner and length derive from per-game win probability with state-dependent updating (injuries, adjustments) and correlation. Cup outcomes follow group tiebreakers (point differential), wildcard rules and single-elimination neutral games. Both require rule-accurate simulation and availability-aware ratings.

player_escalator_payout.label: NBA scalar-payout escalator markets (points/threes)
player_escalator_payout.target: Expected payout of a single-game player stat under a convex payout schedule (e.g. points in 2-point bands, 0-10+ threes)
player_escalator_payout.mechanism: Scalar payouts require the full count distribution, not a single threshold probability; a convex schedule makes the upper tail dominate value. The distribution is a mixture over minutes scenarios with overdispersed attempts and make rates. Settlement tables are in rules_primary and differ by series. Value arises where the market schedule over- or under-weights extreme counts relative to a calibrated tail model.
